questions.q: What two things must be configured together on a secondary replica for automatic failover to be possible?
options: Synchronous commit mode and automatic failover mode
Asynchronous commit mode and manual failover mode
Readable secondary and Basic Availability Group mode
Automatic seeding and FULL recovery model
questions.explain: SQL Server only allows automatic failover mode to be paired with synchronous commit — this pairing is enforced, not optional.

questions.q: What T-SQL command performs a clean, no-data-loss planned failover against a synchronous secondary?
options: ALTER AVAILABILITY GROUP [AG_Sales] FAILOVER;
ALTER AVAILABILITY GROUP [AG_Sales] FORCE_FAILOVER_ALLOW_DATA_LOSS;
DROP AVAILABILITY GROUP [AG_Sales];
ALTER DATABASE [SalesDB] SET HADR OFF;
questions.explain: A plain FAILOVER command, run on a synchronous secondary, performs a planned failover with no data loss since the secondary is already caught up.

questions.q: What does FORCE_FAILOVER_ALLOW_DATA_LOSS explicitly acknowledge, per this lesson?
options: That data committed since the last hardened log record on the target (typically asynchronous) secondary may be lost
That the WSFC cluster will be permanently disbanded
That the database will be converted to SIMPLE recovery model
That the listener will be permanently removed from the AG
questions.explain: Forcing failover to a secondary that isn't fully caught up (usually asynchronous) means accepting that recent transactions might not have replicated yet.

questions.q: Why might automatic failover NOT occur even with a healthy synchronous, automatic-failover-mode secondary available?
options: If the WSFC cluster has lost quorum, it deliberately refuses to fail over automatically to avoid a split-brain scenario
Automatic failover always occurs regardless of quorum status
Because the listener's DNS cache hasn't expired yet
Because the secondary's database is in SIMPLE recovery model
questions.explain: Quorum is a prerequisite for the cluster to safely make any failover decision; without it, the cluster will not promote a secondary even if that secondary is otherwise ready.

questions.q: A primary fails, and the only surviving secondary is asynchronous. Can the AG fail over automatically, and what must a DBA do to bring it back online?
options: No — automatic failover requires synchronous commit; the DBA must run FORCE_FAILOVER_ALLOW_DATA_LOSS, explicitly accepting the risk of losing recently committed data
Yes — any secondary, sync or async, can fail over automatically by default
The DBA should run a plain FAILOVER command, which works safely on asynchronous replicas too
Nothing can be done — an asynchronous secondary can never become primary
questions.explain: Since the secondary is asynchronous, automatic failover isn't possible; a forced manual failover is required, and it comes with an explicit acknowledgment of potential data loss.
